description: Committee recommends early procurement for 60% of 2027-2028 water and sewer projects.
This two-year pilot allows earlier contract awards.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
40% of program funding remains available for future budget deliberations.
Mayor Block asked how early procurement could be an economic support.
Contractors gain more time to bid, plan work, and secure resources.
Exemption to policy: procurement without an approved budget.
Letter from the Construction Association of Saskatchewan attached to the item.
Administration will monitor pilot results and report back to Council in 2028.

description: Noise bylaw extended for six 2026 special events.
Prairieland Park, Shakespeare site events extended until 11:59 p.m.
Brighton, Kinsmen Parks events extended until 7:00 or 10:00 p.m.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Events without three-year history require committee approval for extensions.
Nearby condo residents will be notified of late-night events.
Shakespeare on the Saskatchewan supported extensions, citing revenue and neighbor communication.

speakers.name: Terresa Strohan
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Noise Bylaw Extension Requests
said: Supports noise bylaw extensions for Treehouse and Factor 8 events.
Event revenue is critical for operations and site maintenance.
Strengthening event management, including proactive neighbor communication.

description: City will apply for federal funding to electrify its vehicle fleet.

Project costs $1.7 million, reducing carbon by 3,000 tons.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Project estimated at $1.704 million, funded by FCM grants, loans, and reserves.
Reduces carbon emissions by almost 3,000 tons of CO2E over 10 years.
Fuel and maintenance savings projected to offset loan repayment costs.

description: Committee recommends utility funding for multi-unit garbage.
Program shifts from taxes to utility January 1, 2028.
Rates based on bin size; $121 to $229 monthly.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Estimated 2028 operating requirement is $2.75 million.
Mayor Block questioned why the program could not start sooner.
Properties not using city service will not pay utility.
Administration will continue rate modeling and communication with owners.

description: A strategic framework for climate action is recommended for Council approval.
It includes net zero and climate resilience playbooks.
Future funding for initiatives requires Council approval.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Mayor Block and Councillor Timon praised the report's clarity and comprehensive nature.
Strategy prioritizes low-income households for grants, rebates, and incentive programs.
Saskatoon Climate Hub and SOS Trees Coalition expressed support for the strategy.
Strategy includes actions for Indigenous-led housing, training, and climate solutions.
Strategy aims for net zero by 2050, improving air quality and managing natural infrastructure.
Administration will report on climate action progress every two years.

speakers.name: Caroline Dinter
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Climate Action Strategy
said: Supports the strategy, highlighting the urban forest's importance.
Recommends reinstating opt-out policy for boulevard tree planting.
Advocates for private tree planting incentives and natural area conservation.

speakers.name: Carroll Chubb
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: The Climate Action Strategy
said: Urges council to adopt and adequately fund the strategy.
Supports increasing energy efficiency standards and resilient infrastructure.
Advocates for grid-scale battery storage and renewable energy projects.

chips.text: Recommended to Council

Administration will report back to Council in 2026 with negotiation update, options.
